recognize_zh: 周邊血液中的母細胞胞質深藍，邊緣呈毛邊狀、拉出細絲或泡狀突起（cytoplasmic blebs/pseudopods），其中一顆胞質內有空泡；這種帶胞質突起的母細胞是巨核母細胞的經典外觀，在唐氏症病童即 ML-DS。
features: Medium-sized blasts with round nuclei, high N:C ratio and finely granular chromatin
Deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm with frayed borders, blebs and thread-like projections
Background red cells largely normocytic without nucleated forms in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several circulating blasts. The blasts are medium-sized with round nuclei, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios and finely granular chromatin, and they have deeply basophilic agranular cytoplasm with irregular frayed borders, cytoplasmic blebs, thread-like projections and an occasional vacuole. Background red cells are unremarkable in this field. The cytoplasmic blebbing is characteristic of megakaryoblasts; in a child with Down syndrome, the findings are consistent with myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome, pending CD41/CD61 immunophenotyping.

ddx.vs: Indistinguishable blasts; TAM occurs in the first weeks of life and regresses without therapy.
Lymphoblasts have smooth cytoplasmic outlines without blebs and lack platelet glycoprotein expression.
Hairy cells have circumferential fine hair-like projections but mature oval nuclei with open chromatin and pale gray-blue cytoplasm, and are CD11c/CD103/annexin A1-positive B cells in adults.
